references.text: Jesus went up the mountain to pray in solitude, which shows the same pattern of withdrawing to pray alone.
Mark tells us that Jesus got up early in the morning and went out to a deserted place to pray, which is a direct parallel to Jesus' habit of withdrawing for prayer.
Luke again tells us that Jesus went up the mountain to pray and spent the whole night in prayer to God—a recurring pattern in Jesus' life.
Jesus was alone and prayed, showing the same pattern of withdrawal and prayer as in Luke 5:16.
Jesus was in a certain place praying, and his disciples asked him to teach them how to pray—yet another example of Jesus' prayer life.
In Gethsemane, Jesus withdrew from his disciples to pray, showing the deep need for solitary prayer, especially in difficult times.
Jesus went away to a deserted place, and the crowds tried to hold him back. This shows the same pattern of seeking solitude after great activity among the people.
The immediate context: news about Jesus spread, and large crowds came to hear him and be healed. The verses are closely linked—the pressure from the crowds explains why Jesus withdrew.
After saying goodbye to the crowd, Jesus went up the mountain to pray—again the same pattern of withdrawing to lonely places for prayer.
Isaiah encourages going into a quiet room and closing the door—an Old Testament example of withdrawing to seek God in silence.
Jesus teaches his disciples to go into their inner room and pray to their Father in secret, which reflects his own practice of withdrawing to pray.
